specs.note: min – max · NG label max differs

steps: Plan the location
Into an existing wall, a corner, a built-in wall or a wall projection. Keep it out of traffic, away from furniture and draperies, and accessible for service.

Decide where the unit goes, the vent route and where the gas supply will be plumbed. Install to local codes or, in their absence, the National Fuel Gas Code ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 or the National Gas and Propane Installation Code CSA B149.1 (p. 15). Manufactured (USA only) or mobile home OEM installs: Title 24 CFR, Part 3280, or ANSI/NCSBCS A225.1, or CSA Z240.4.

  • May be installed in an aftermarket permanently located manufactured home (USA only) or mobile home, where not prohibited by local codes.
  • Must not be connected to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.
  • Not for use with air filters (rating label, p. 51).
Note: the cover (p. 1) says the appliance is suitable for installation in a bedroom or bed sitting room; the rating label (p. 51) says "In Canada, also certified for installation in a bedroom or a bedsitting room."

Overall dimensions and vent-location dimensions are shown only as drawings (pp. 15–16).
Top or rear vent outlet
To vent out the rear, remove the outer collar (5 Torx T20 screws) and the cover plate (5 screws), rotate the flue to the rear, and refit plate and collar with their gaskets.

1. Remove the outer collar (5 Torx T20 screws).
  2. Remove the 5 screws holding the cover plate.
  3. Remove the screws holding the flue to the unit; carefully remove the flue and the gasket.
  4. Rotate the flue to point out the rear. With the gasket in place, install and tighten the screws.
  5. Re-install the cover plate with the solid gasket on the top of the unit.
  6. Place the outer collar and gasket around the flue, center it and re-install the screws.

Chase height minimums differ by outlet: 54" top vented, 50" rear vented (p. 19).
Frame the enclosure
Chase 36" wide × 16" deep, 54" high top-vented or 50" rear-vented, 0" standoffs. Mount the steel framing kit, add a 2 x 4 header flush with it, and screw the unit to the framing.

Recommended: set the fireplace in place and install the venting before framing in the enclosure (p. 19). Finishing material must not interfere with glass door and safety screen removal. Minimum dimensions must include drywall or non-combustible board if installed.

Framing kit

  1. Place the facing support panel, edge with the three holes in the middle down, on top of the outer casing; align the holes and attach with five screws from the underside.
  2. Assemble the kit (2 horizontal pieces, 2 vertical pieces, 8 screws): screw the top piece through the holes toward the edge, the bottom piece through the middle holes and those closest to one edge.
  3. Set the kit, offset screws down, on the facing support panel; align the holes and attach with five screws.
  4. Push the unit tight against the framing stops; the included steel stud framing installs flush with the framing. Secure with wood screws; the tabs sit flush against the framing.
  5. Install a 2 x 4 header on top of the steel framing kit, front edge flush with the kit.

Insulation

Against an uninsulated exterior wall or chase, insulate to the same degree as other exterior walls and cover insulation and vapor barrier with a solid surface such as drywall; never place the fireplace directly against them. Do not insulate the front of the chase between the top of the fireplace and the top of the supplied steel studs.
Vent and terminate

4" x 6-5/8" coaxial only, inside the NG or LP venting chart: 40 feet max total, max three 90° elbows, 3" to combustibles. Approved Duravent or ICC terminal; install the damper and set it per the chart.

• Any rise and run combination inside the chart for the fuel: NG on p. 23, LP on p. 24. The zones are drawn as a graph, so read them there.
  • One 90° elbow (or elbows equaling 90°) without reducing the horizontal run; reduce the horizontal run by 2 feet for each additional 90°.
  • Horizontal venting may be supported by non-combustible supports; ensure the vent pipe is properly supported. Fire stops wherever the vent passes through a wall, floor or ceiling.
  • Vertical: Duravent 46DVA-VCH or ICC TM-4" SVT. Horizontal: Duravent 46DVA-HSCH or ICC TM-4"HT (p. 27). Terminal clearances: p. 26.

Damper kit (pp. 45–46)

  1. Remove the screen and door. Remove the 4 screws across the top of the angled back shield and pull it gently forward off its retainers to expose the flue opening.
  2. Install the mounting plate (3 screws), pressed-in nuts on the top side, then the sliding damper plate (2 bolts).
  3. Loosen the two bolts (3/8), slide the plate to the numbered notch the chart calls for, and tighten.
  4. Re-install the rear shield: slide it into the retainers, tilt the front up and install the 4 screws.
The chart's damper positions were set in controlled testing and are a general guideline; a setting may need slight adjustment. The damper mechanism may be hot if the fireplace has been burning.
Electrical connection
House wire through the strain relief on the left side, joined to the unit harness with wire nuts; both grounds to the Ground Post. Qualified electrician, local code.

Electrical rating: 115V, 60hz, 1.2 A (rating label copy, p. 51).

Pass the house wire through the strain relief on the left-hand side of the fireplace and connect it to the wires inside with wire nuts. Connect the ground wire from the house wire and the unit harness to the Ground Post. Electrical connections should be performed by a qualified electrician as per local electrical codes.
Gas connection + leak test
Pipe to the 3/8" NPT shut-off on the right side with a drip leg ahead of the control valve. Check all connections tight and leak free, bleed the lines, and make the first start with the door removed.

• Gas line by a qualified service person to all building codes. Use the correct supply line diameter to assure proper operation and pressure.
  • The valve is shut off when the handle is in the "down" or "across" position.
  • Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve from the supply piping during any pressure test of that system in excess of 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa) (p. 4).
  • Leak (sniff) test after any gas connection, gas valve or pilot assembly is replaced or serviced, with a detector that can detect natural gas and propane.
  • Disconnect power at the circuit breaker before and during gas valve or connection work; don't reconnect it until the leak test has ruled out a leak.

Servicing can be performed from the front of the unit.
Propane conversion (if LP)

Gas and power off, unit cool: fit the #ES orifice, set the pilot band to propane, convert the SIT valve per its kit and apply the conversion label. Open the venturi fully and confirm manifold pressure.

By a qualified service agency, using the factory-supplied components (parts list: LP Conversion Kit, z25 · 12180010, p. 52).

  1. Shut off the gas supply and electrical power; let the appliance cool.
  2. With the burner removed, use a ½" deep socket to remove the natural gas orifice from the venturi box. Fit the #ES orifice (the #ET is only for the glass burner vented out the rear) with a small amount of sealing cement.
  3. Pilot: loosen the pilot head slightly with a 7/16" wrench, slide the adjustment band so the hole in the band is showing (propane position), then gently re-tighten.
  4. Valve: follow the instruction book in the SIT conversion kit. Remove the screw holding the control module plate, slide plate and module out, and remove the module cover plate to reach the module and the servo connector.
  5. Fill in the date and name on the conversion label and apply it to the module cover plate; re-install the cover screw, push the mounting plate back and install the locking screw.
  6. Set the venturi adjustment to fully open (it ships fully closed for natural gas, p. 44).
  7. Confirm proper manifold pressure (p. 33). The conversion is not complete until the converted appliance's operation is checked per the kit instructions.

The conversion label shown on p. 32 carries kit number 5052.52001-B.
Gas pressure test
With the fireplace lit at its highest setting, gauge the inlet and manifold test ports on the SIT valve. Gas off before loosening a test-port screw, and retighten after.

1. Remove the window screen / surround; locate the valve and the shut-off valve.
  2. Turn the gas off at the shut-off valve.
  3. Loosen the screw in the inlet or manifold test port and attach the tube from a pressure gauge.
  4. Turn the gas supply back on and verify the pressure.
  5. Turn the gas off, remove the gauge and tighten the test-port screw.
Inlet NG / LP5.0 – 7.0" WC / 12.5 – 13.9" WC
Manifold NG / LP1.1 – 3.8" WC / 6.4 – 11" WC

The rating label gives different maximums; see the inlet and manifold spec cards.
Facing and finishing
Combustible facing only in zone 1; zone 2, directly above the opening, takes non-combustible materials only. The finishing trim takes wall finishes from 1/2" to 1-1/4.

• Zone 1: drywall or other combustible facing materials.
  • Zone 2, directly above the fireplace opening: non-combustible materials and finishes only, such as masonry or calcium silicate board and tile or stone. Zone sizes are shown only in the drawing on p. 34.
  • Remove the 4 screws holding the adjustable finishing trim; it accommodates wall finishes from 1/2" to 1-1/4 (12mm to 32mm).
  • Facing material may be 1/4" to flush with the inside edges of the fireplace casing. Do not place any material over the opening around the door.
  • Once the facing is complete, re-install the finishing trim against the wall and tighten the screws.

Above the fireplace, non-combustible board must reach a minimum of 21-5/8" [55cm] above the opening or the top of the steel framing kit (p. 19).
Panels, log set and screen
Fit any optional liner panels first, then the ember bed, logs, glass media and vermiculite in order, checking the ember lights with the burner off. Hang the safety screen before use.

Optional liner sets (pp. 36–38): 3pc black porcelain coated steel, 4 pc ledge stone, 3pc fluted or 4pc red brick ceramic fiber. Install them before the burner media tray; for fluted or red brick, bend the spacer tabs up 90 degrees. Fiber panels are fragile: trim slightly rather than force them.

Log set (pp. 39–41)

  1. With the ember tray installed, insert the front trim piece. Turn on the ember lights from the remote (not the burner) to check every light after transport.
  2. Large ember bed in the center of the burner tubes; an ember chunk on each point along the tray edge; a few chunks along the valley; pulled ember fluff between the chunks.
  3. Rear log on the bent-over tabs, pushed against the rear panel and centered; right and left logs over the pins in the rear log, ends not past the door opening.
  4. Amber glass media spread along the front of the tray; vermiculite lightly over the glass.
  5. Front left and front right logs over their pins; left and right ember pieces on the glass; center twig from the ember bed to the pad on the front left log, resting against the front right log.

Door, screen and start-up

Door: hooks into the pivot slots on the firebox floor, push the top in, engage the catches (p. 43). Screen: lower hooks into the floor slots, then push the top in so the upper tabs fit over the mounting hooks (p. 42). Venturi: the screw under the door on the right adjusts flame appearance; clockwise closes, counterclockwise opens (p. 44).

Start-up (p. 8): 4 AA batteries in the battery holder with its switch on "Remote", 3 AAA in the transmitter, power on and gas open; press PRG once (3 beeps), then the transmitter power button once (4 beeps = synchronized).

Barrier part numbers: the rating label reads "For use only with barrier part #100004568" (p. 51); the parts list gives Screen Assembly, z25 as 80002641 (p. 52).

panels.title: Burner won't light
items: First lighting: air has to escape from the lines first
Not lit → On/Off to off, wait minimum 5 minutes; if you still smell gas, stop; if not, try again
Gas smell after waiting → stop; follow the gas-smell steps
Won't light or stay lit after several tries → off, all electric power off, call the service technician or gas supplier

panels.title: Low or dead batteries
items: Battery icon on the transmitter display → remote batteries (3 AAA) low
IFC double-beeps when it receives a command → IFC batteries (4 AA) low
Receiver or transmitter batteries low or depleted → turn off with the ON/OFF switch on the battery box

panels.title: Soot / flame pattern
items: Excessive soot on media or burner → qualified service person inspects and adjusts for proper combustion
Flame pattern or sooting → minor venturi adjustment (clockwise closes, counterclockwise opens)
Venturi preset fully closed for natural gas; set fully open for propane

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace has an ignition device that lights the pilot for you. Never try to light the pilot by hand. You light it with the remote.

Before you light it

Smell all around the fireplace for gas, including down next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety and gas smell.

To light it

  1. Push the On/Off button on the remote. A single beep from the fireplace confirms it got the command.
  2. If the burner lights, use the remote to set the flame and other settings.
  3. If it doesn't light, push On/Off again to turn it off. Wait at least 5 minutes so any gas in the firebox can clear. If you still smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety and gas smell. If you don't smell gas, try step 1 again.
  4. If it won't light or stay lit after several tries, turn it off with the remote, turn off all electric power to the fireplace, and call your service technician or gas supplier.
The very first lighting can take longer, because air has to escape from the gas lines first.
Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs on 3 AAA batteries. Each time the fireplace receives a command, it answers with a single beep.

The keys

  • On/Off turns the fireplace on or off. When it's off, the display shows only the room temperature.
  • Up / Down arrows set the flame: there are six levels. Down lowers it one step at a time until the flame goes out. If the system is on but the flame is off, up brings it back on high.
  • Thermostat turns on room-thermostat mode; set the temperature with the arrows. Keep pressing until "Smart" appears for Smart mode: it turns the flame down as the room nears your setting and up when the room is cool.
  • Mode steps through the fan, lights and pilot settings.

Handy extras

  • Key lock: press Mode and Up together and a lock icon appears. Do the same to unlock.
  • °F or °C: with the system off, press Thermostat and Mode together, then check the display shows F or C.
  • Pairing (done at setup): press the PRG button on the On/Off switch behind the screen once (3 beeps), then the remote's power button once. Four beeps mean they're paired.
It can turn on suddenly. Keep away from the burner when you use the remote or the manual On/Off switch.

sounds.title: First fire: smells and sounds
sounds.html:
A slight smell at first

The first time you light it, the fireplace gives off a slight odour for a couple of hours. That's the paints, sealants, gaskets and lubricants from manufacturing curing in the heat. It's temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room, because the smell can bother some people.

Ticks and pings

Steel fireplaces make some expansion and contraction noises as they warm up and cool down. Your furnace or kitchen oven makes the same kind of sound. It's normal.

Something else wrong?

If you find any problem with the fireplace, contact your dealer right away to have it repaired. Don't try to repair it yourself: you could hurt yourself or others and damage the unit.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, touch electrical switches or use a phone in the building. Call your gas supplier from a neighbour's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it, using glass cleaner. For touch stains, use a fireplace (ceramic) glass cleaner.

  • Never clean the glass when it's hot.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners on the glass or any other part of the fireplace.
  • The outside finish can be cleaned with mild soap and water.

Look after the glass door

  • Don't strike or knock the glass. It can break.
  • Don't run the fireplace with the glass door removed, cracked or broken. Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the fireplace again.
  • Replacement doors come from your Pacific Energy dealer. Don't substitute any other type, and have a licensed or qualified service person fit it.
  • The glass gasket keeps the seal in good condition. It should be checked and replaced if necessary.

extras.title: Fan, lights and pilot mode
extras.html:
These settings sit behind the Mode key on the remote. Press Mode until you reach the icon you want, then use the arrow keys. A single beep confirms each change.

Comfort fan

If your fireplace has the air-circulating fan, go to the fan icon. Use the arrows to turn it on or off and choose one of six speeds.

Maker's website: Blower, 120 cfm Variable Speed Blower included (Standard Features).

Overhead accent light

Go to the AUX icon. Up turns the light on; down turns it off.

Ember-bed lights

Go to the light-bulb icon. Use the arrows to set the glow; there are six levels.

Pilot mode: IPI or CPI

With the system off, go to the CPI icon. Up switches on continuous pilot ignition (CPI); down returns to intermittent pilot ignition (IPI).

The overhead light uses a halogen lamp that may need replacing on occasion. The steps start with removing the safety screen and glass door (p. 49). Wear gloves: bare fingers leave oil on the lamp and shorten its life.

power.title: Power and batteries
power.html:
Your fireplace runs on house power. A battery pack backs up the control, so it can keep working when the house power is interrupted or lost.

Fireplace battery holder4 AA
Remote3 AAA

The battery holder sits behind the screen/surround, below the firebox. Keep its selection switch on Remote.

Signs of low batteries

  • Remote: a battery icon shows on the display before the power runs out. It goes away once you put in new batteries.
  • Fireplace: it double-beeps when it receives a command. With new batteries, it goes back to a single beep.

Battery life depends on the battery quality, how often the fireplace lights, and how often you change the thermostat setting.

Batteries dead? You can still turn the fireplace off with the On/Off switch on the battery box, at the lower front behind the screen.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
To turn the fireplace off, push the On/Off button on the remote. The display then shows only the room temperature, and the fireplace beeps once to confirm.

For service or a long shutdown

After turning it off with the remote, turn off all electric power to the fireplace and remove the backup batteries. Do this before service is done, or when it will be shut down for a long time.

If the remote won't work

If the batteries in the remote or the fireplace are low or dead, you can turn the fireplace off by hand with the On/Off switch on the battery box, at the lower front behind the screen. This bypasses the remote.

Keep clear of the burner when you use the remote or the manual switch. The fireplace can turn on suddenly.
Before any servicing, the gas and electrical power are turned off and the fireplace is given plenty of time to cool.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbour's phone and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.
  • Installation and service must be done by a qualified installer, service agency or the gas supplier.

Around the fireplace

  • The surfaces get very hot. Make sure children and adults know the risk of burns and clothing catching fire, and stay back.
  • Supervise young children in the same room. If anyone at risk lives with you, a physical barrier is recommended; an adjustable safety gate can keep toddlers out of the room.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, draperies and anything flammable away. Don't store or use gasoline or other flammable vapours and liquids near it.
  • The mesh safety screen must stay installed. If it gets damaged, replace it with the manufacturer's barrier for this fireplace.
  • Put back any grill, panel or door removed for service before you use it.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected before use and at least once a year by a qualified service person, and have the venting checked too. Installation and repair are jobs for a qualified service person.

What the yearly check covers

  • Removing the glass door and the logs, embers and glass media to look for soot. Heavy soot means the unit needs adjusting for proper combustion.
  • Cleaning the burner with a brush or vacuum, paying close attention to the burner ports.
  • Checking the pilot flame size and operation, and cleaning the pilot.
  • Making sure the vent pipe and vent terminal are open and free of blockage or debris.
  • Checking the batteries and replacing them as needed.
Lots of lint? More frequent cleaning may be needed if there's a lot of lint from carpeting, bedding and the like. The control compartment, burners and air passages must be kept clean.

Keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that burns, and of gasoline and other flammable vapours and liquids.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
NG min / max5.0" WC / 7.0" WC

From the gas pressure requirements table (p. 33). The rating label's minimum supply pressures agree: NG 5.00 in/wc (1.24 kPa), LP 12.50 in/wc (3.11 kPa).

Note: the pressure table on p. 33 gives a natural-gas maximum supply pressure of 7.0" WC; the rating label on p. 51 gives 13.90 in/wc (3.46 kPa).

Verify with the fireplace lit and at the highest setting, at the inlet pressure test point on the SIT valve. Turn off the gas supply at the appliance before loosening the test-port screw. Disconnect the appliance during supply-piping pressure tests in excess of 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa).

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
NG high / low3.8" WC / 1.1" WC

From the gas pressure requirements table (p. 33). Test at the manifold pressure test point on the SIT valve with the fireplace lit at the highest setting. After a propane conversion, confirm proper manifold pressure.

Note: the table on p. 33 gives a maximum manifold pressure of 3.8" WC (NG) and 11" WC (LP); the rating label on p. 51 gives a maximum of 3.50 in/wc (0.87 kPa) for NG and 10.00 in/wc (2.49 kPa) for LP.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Direct vent, top or rear outlet (field conversion, p. 17). Certified for use with 4" x 6-5/8" coaxial venting components only; mixing venting components from different manufacturers is inadvisable.

Max total length40 feet
90° elbowsMax three
Horizontal runReduce 2 feet per 90° after the first
To combustibles3" [75mm] min

Any rise and run combination inside the NG chart (p. 23) or LP chart (p. 24). Fire stops wherever the vent passes through a wall, floor or ceiling. Terminals: Duravent 46DVA-VCH or ICC TM-4" SVT (vertical), Duravent 46DVA-HSCH or ICC TM-4"HT (horizontal); no others are approved (p. 27).

A damper kit ships with the fireplace. The charts show, by rise and run, whether no damper, an open damper, a numbered damper position or (NG only) a closed damper applies. The zones are drawn as a graph, so read them on pp. 23–24, then set the sliding plate to that numbered notch (p. 46).

specTerm.title: Vent terminal clearances
specTerm.html:
Minimums from the terminal, US column of the table, with Canada values where they differ. The lettered locations are shown in a drawing on p. 26.

A · above grass, plants, deck, porch, balcony12 inches
B · beside or below a window or door that opens9 inches (Canada 12 inches)
C · permanently closed window9 inches
D · ventilated soffit within 2 feet of center line14 inches
E · unventilated soffit14 inches
F · outside corner6 inches
G · inside corner14 inches
J · non-mechanical air inlet, other appliance's combustion air9 inches (Canada 12 inches)
K · mechanical air supply inlet3 feet (Canada 6 feet)
M · under veranda, porch, deck, balcony12 inches

H (beside the meter/regulator), I (service regulator vent) and L (above a public paved sidewalk or driveway): US per local codes and the gas supplier; Canada 3 feet, 3 feet and 7 feet. The L row also carries a footnote: a vent shall not terminate directly above a sidewalk or paved driveway which is located between two single family dwellings and serves both dwellings. The K row also carries "above if within 10ft (3m) horizontally". M is permitted only if the veranda, porch, deck or balcony is fully open on a minimum of two sides beneath the floor.

Massachusetts: a side-wall terminal less than seven (7) feet above finished grade needs CO detectors and a vent sign at least eight (8) feet above grade (p. 3).

specElec.title: Electrical connection
specElec.html:
Electrical rating115V, 60hz, 1.2 A

Rating from the rating label (copy on p. 51). Pass the house wire through the strain relief on the left-hand side of the fireplace and connect it to the unit's wiring harness with wire nuts; connect the ground wire from the house wire and the unit harness to the Ground Post. Qualified electrician, per local electrical codes.

The Proflame 2 IFC runs on AC with a battery pack for backup (4 AA, p. 8). Disconnect power at the circuit breaker before and during gas valve or gas connection work.

Shock hazard: the IFC is powered by line voltage. Do not open or tamper with its enclosure; disconnect line voltage before any maintenance (p. 12).

index_extra.p: What to do if you smell gas
Turn it off, wait at least 5 minutes; if you still smell gas, stop; if not, try again
Battery icon on the remote, double-beep from the fireplace
Key lock: press Mode and Up together
Comfort fan: six speeds from the remote
Numbered damper notch from the NG / LP venting chart
ES orifice, pilot band, SIT valve kit

conflicts.issue: Exposed-sidewall clearance from center of window: 18" [46cm] in the chase clearances (p. 19) vs 22" [56cm] in the clearance drawing (p. 35) and 22.00 in (559 mm) 'Center to sidewall' on the rating label (p. 51). Flagged in specClear and specChase.
Natural-gas maximum supply pressure: 7.0" WC in the gas pressure requirements table (p. 33) vs 13.90 in/wc on the rating label (p. 51).
Maximum manifold pressure: 3.8" WC NG / 11" WC LP in the table (p. 33) vs 3.50 in/wc NG / 10.00 in/wc LP on the rating label (p. 51).

Bedroom installation: cover (p. 1) says suitable for installation in a bedroom or bed sitting room with no country limit; the rating label (p. 51) says 'In Canada, also certified for installation in a bedroom or a bedsitting room'.

catalog_mismatches.catalog: 120 cfm Variable Speed Blower included (Standard Features)
catalog_mismatches.manual: Blower, Gas, (optional on some models) in the parts list (p. 52); "If the fireplace is equipped with an air circulating fan", six (6) speeds (p. 11); no cfm given

review.notes: Checked catalog BTU (NG 25,000/13,500, LP 24,000/13,500), efficiency (71.7 / 69.1, P.4.1), vent size (4 x 6-5/8), mobile-home approval and IPI/CPI: all match the manual (pp. 25, 30, 51). The website's blower ('120 cfm Variable Speed Blower included (Standard Features)') is shown as a website note in extras: the parts list says 'Blower, Gas, (optional on some models)' (p. 52), p. 11 says 'If the fireplace is equipped with an air circulating fan', and no cfm is given. The manual never says 'Tofino' or 'Premium' (cover: 'z25 (w' Log Burner)'); title uses the catalog name shortened to fit. LP data shown for the log burner (ES orifice); the ET orifice is for the glass burner. No warranty terms in this manual (p. 4 only says deviations void the warranty), so no warranty tile. No troubleshooting chart or code table: fault panels come from the lighting instructions (p. 14), low-battery detection (p. 12) and the annual-inspection / venturi text (pp. 13, 44); beep signals (pp. 8-12) are in drawers and codes is empty. Figures not transcribed: dimension drawing (p. 15), vent-location drawing (p. 16), NG/LP venting-chart zones (pp. 23-24), '3' Min' in Fig. 35 (p. 25), the vent-terminal location drawing (p. 26), facing-zone drawing (p. 34; its 20-3/4" may or may not correspond to the 21-5/8" non-combustible minimum on p. 19) and the clearance drawing beyond its mantel table (p. 35). Text oddities: p. 25 says venting must be 'certified to current ????? standards'; p. 29 points to 'the chart on page 33' for the input rating, but inputs are on pp. 30 and 51; p. 4 says to isolate the appliance at test pressures 'equal to or greater than 1/2 psi' (the disconnect rule is 'in excess of 1/2 psi'), so only the disconnect rule is shown; chase height is 'from floor' on p. 19 but 'measured from bottom of unit' on p. 20; chase depth 16" is [405mm] on p. 19 and [406mm] on p. 20; the vent-terminal K row's 'above if within 10ft (3m) horizontally' is not clearly in the US or Canada column. Part numbers to confirm: the rating label says 'For use only with barrier part #100004568' while the parts list gives Screen Assembly, z25 as 80002641; the conversion label shows kit number 5052.52001-B while the parts list gives LP Conversion Kit, z25 as 12180010 under 'Options', though p. 30 says to convert 'using the components supplied with this fireplace'.
